key_insight: Asymmetric electron–defect scattering can generate a substantial extrinsic photovoltaic current that peaks at a finite defect fraction.
engineering_relevance: Controlling defect type and concentration could provide a tunable route to enhanced photocurrent in monolayer GeS.
method: Develop an ab initio Boltzmann framework for optically excited carriers.
Include electron–phonon scattering and symmetric and skew electron–defect scattering.
Evaluate monolayer GeS across defect fractions and temperatures.
evidence_signal: The calculations predict over six orders of magnitude enhancement upon cooling to 0 K at fixed defect fraction, with extrinsic current exceeding intrinsic shift current by over tenfold at selected low-temperature defect fractions.
watch_item: The enhancements are predictions within a scattering-limited model, not demonstrated device performance, and the largest gains rely on low-temperature conditions.
paper_title: Extrinsic Bulk Photovoltaic Effect from Asymmetric Defect Scattering
